name: BPC-157

lead: BPC-157 ("body protection compound 157") is a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide modeled on a fragment of a protein found in human gastric juice. It has no approved medical use anywhere and is sold mainly as a "research chemical" and through compounding channels.

In appearance and recovery circles it is promoted for tendon, ligament, gut and wound healing, on the argument that faster repair supports training and aesthetics. The supporting literature comes overwhelmingly from rodent experiments, largely from a single research group, and a 2025 systematic review found almost no human clinical data.

paras: Preclinical work suggests BPC-157 may influence angiogenesis (including VEGF signaling), growth-hormone receptor expression in tendon fibroblasts, nitric oxide pathways and the FAK-paxillin axis, which together could speed cell migration and tissue repair. These mechanisms are proposed from cell and animal studies and have not been confirmed in controlled human trials.

Human safety data are minimal, so the risk profile is largely unknown. Concerns include unregulated product purity and identity, injection-site problems, and a theoretical concern that pro-angiogenic activity could be undesirable in people with cancer risk. It is not FDA-approved, US regulators have flagged evidence and safety gaps for compounding, and it is prohibited by WADA for tested athletes.
